conviction_note: No document turned up a number the street lacks. Three small sourced reads lean slightly negative: Q3 deposit-cost and NIM pressure (FHN's own Q2 spot rate plus Nashville peer FBK's Oct 13 print), softer mortgage warehouse and utilization (CEO at Barclays, Sep 15), and a Sep 16 Fed hike that helps an asset-sensitive book while hurting the counter-cyclical fixed-income desk. This name has sold its last two beats (-9.4% on an expense miss in Oct 2025, -3.0% on deposit costs in Jul 2026), so p_up is 45 on an abs_move of 3.0, giving -0.3 against an impact_sum of -0.4. The stock is already -6% over 20 days and -7.4% since the July print, and the lean may be the pessimism artefact LESSONS warns about, so the number is kept small.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $0.52-0.53 on revenue of about $891-893M (Benzinga snapshots through 2026-10-06, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FHN/earnings-forecasts; AAII 2026-10-12 also gives $0.52, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514985-what-you-need-to-know-about-first-horizon-corporations-q3-earnings). Chartmill gives $0.55 on $912.3M (https://www.chartmill.com/news/FHN/Chartmill-50996-First-Horizon-Corp-NYSEFHN-Beats-Q2-Earnings-Estimates-Showing-Steady-Profitability-Improvement), so the sources disagree slightly and every finding is capped small. Company guide for FY2026, reiterated 2026-07-15: adjusted revenue +3-7%, adjusted expenses roughly flat, NCO 15-25 bp (https://pulse2.com/first-horizon-brokered-deposits-jump-47-as-commercial-loan-growth-pressures-margin/). print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS: FHN beat EPS on each of the last three prints, and the share count is down 7% YoY.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 10.6M shares, 1.9 days to cover, at the 2026-08-14 settlement, down from 14.3M (2.2 days) on 2026-07-31 (FINRA via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fhn/short-interest/). That is roughly 2% of about 470M shares outstanding, so the short is not crowded. Millennium filed a 13G showing 5.6% as of 2026-09-28. Skew is unavailable: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 91% of mid). Put/call OI is 1.12 on 2,867 contracts, too thin to read. Tape: -5.95% over 20 days, -14.2% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: FHN's own Q2 release put the period-end spot rate on interest-bearing deposits at about 2.43%, against a 2.33% quarterly average and with brokered CDs up $2B. Nashville competitor FB Financial reported on 2026-10-13: cost of interest-bearing deposits up 7 bp to 2.88% and NIM down 12 bp to 3.83% on higher funding costs. Both point to a Q3 interest-bearing deposit cost about 10 bp higher and NIM pressure below Q2's 3.49%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print (2026-07-15) beat EPS ($0.54 vs $0.52) but NIM fell 3 bp on brokered-deposit costs. Shares fell 3.85% intraday (allmind/Investing.com) and -3.03% in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: FBK printed only yesterday, after FHN last spoke (Barclays, 2026-09-15), so estimates set before then may not carry a ~10 bp step-up. It is likely partly priced: the spot rate was in FHN's own July release, and the stock is -7.4% since that print. If it were fully priced, the bar would sit below Q2's $0.54 by more than the $0.01-0.02 it does.
findings.independence: Two documents: FHN's Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q2026earningsrelease.htm, spot rate 2.43%) and FBK's Q3 release. At Barclays the CEO said Q3 deposit growth was supported by incentives (https://quartr.com/events/first-horizon-corporation-fhn-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3sp4maWq, secondary summary). FBK is a peer proxy, not FHN's number.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-15, CEO Bryan Jordan said mortgage warehouse lending had softened on higher rates and line utilization was drifting down. Loans to mortgage companies were $4.76B at Q2 end, about 7% of $65.3B in loans, and they carry a high yield. Wells Fargo's 2026-10-13 release shows Home Lending revenue down 2% QoQ.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print isolates the warehouse line. In Q2 loans to mortgage companies rose $118M and were not the reaction driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said publicly at an investor conference a month ago, so mostly priced. The residual is the size of the balance decline, which nobody has published. This is sized net of the rest of the book: commercial loans grew about $1.6B in Q2, and the CEO said CRE lending is rebounding and pipelines are strong. That growth on 93% of loans offsets most of the warehouse drag.
findings.independence: Home Lending in Wells Fargo's 2026-10-13 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm) is a broad mortgage-activity proxy. The FHN statement comes from a secondary summary of the webcast.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25 bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. FHN is modestly asset-sensitive (58% variable-rate loans; per its Q2 disclosure, a 100 bp move changes 12-month NII by about 3.3%), so the hike adds roughly 0.8% to forward NII. The same rate rise hurts the counter-cyclical fixed-income desk ($46M in Q2, down $7M QoQ). Last year the Q3 call carried the initial outlook for the next year, so the 2027 outlook on this call will reflect both effects.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q3 2025 call (2025-10-15) the initial 2026 outlook (flat expenses, mid-single-digit loan growth) came with an efficiency-ratio miss, and the stock fell 9.4% (about -12% intraday) despite an EPS beat (https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/stockstory-2025-10-15-why-first-horizon-fhn-stock-is-falling-today). Raymond James then cut its target and noted that lower rates help the counter-cyclical businesses (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/first-horizon-price-target-lowered-to-23-from-25-at-raymond-james-thefly, dated 2025-10-15).
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public. What is not public is how management nets asset sensitivity against weaker fixed-income and warehouse revenue in a 2027 frame. If the market had priced a clean NII tailwind, FHN would not have lagged at -6% over 20 days into a hiking cycle. The two effects offset, so the finding is small and wide.
findings.independence: Asset sensitivity is from FHN's Q2 disclosure, as summarized by https://pulse2.com/first-horizon-brokered-deposits-jump-47-as-commercial-loan-growth-pressures-margin/ (2026-08-02). Fixed-income revenue is from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q2026earningsrelease.htm). The Fed decision is confirmed only by secondary calendars, not the Fed's own statement.

findings.finding: Millennium Management filed a Schedule 13G showing 26.3M FHN shares (5.6%) as of 2026-09-28, up from 23.5M (4.97%) as of 2026-09-01. A multi-strategy fund built a passive stake above 5% into the weakness before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public filing, and pod holdings are usually hedged and carry no direction for the print. It is filed because it is sourced; it is sized at zero.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild negative lean agrees with the -6% 20-day run-up and the name's habit of selling beats, so much of it is probably already in the price, which keeps the size small.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the mortgage-warehouse finding shrank from -0.3 to -0.2, because commercial and CRE loans (about 93% of the book) are growing and offset it
Rule 6 (bar): the EPS bar sources disagree ($0.52-0.53 vs $0.55), so every finding stays capped small; all were already small
Rule 1 (reaction history): this name sold its last two beats, so p_up stays at 45 despite an expected small EPS beat (print_vs_bar +1.5)
Pessimism-artefact note: all three non-zero leans are negative or near zero, so the negative findings were not enlarged; everything else is unchanged
